contentCorrections.DISDATA212: Develops generic image representation,filtering,segmentation,feature detection,tracking andclassification with Python/OpenCV andout-of-sample evaluation. Provides specific image-analysis methods for the evidenced health-technology concept; a required medical-imaging ordiagnostic application is not established by the current course.
contentCorrections.DISDATA211: Develops statistical learning,prediction/classification,model accuracy,resampling andevaluation onrealdata. These methods specifically support evaluating health-technology evidence; no dedicated medical dataset orclinical AI course is assumed.
contentCorrections.GOSPHIL212: Develops historical andcontemporary moral theories,close reading andethical argument. Provides a specific normative foundation for assessing prevention,responsibility andfair healthcare; no medical-ethics practicum orprescribed healthcare case is assumed.
contentCorrections.HCBLIFE214: Provides hands-on blood analysis,microbial culture/hygiene,transformation,GFPproduction/purification,DNAanalysis andintroductory bioinformatics withreproducible lab records. Direct biomedical research-method contribution; not clinical diagnostic qualification.
contentCorrections.HCBPSYC313: Develops systematic review,study selection,bias appraisal,effect sizes andfixed/random-effects meta-analysis inR,including heterogeneity,moderators andpublication bias. A small group meta-analysis andposter support evidence synthesis; it is not anindependent clinical thesis.
contentCorrections.HCBBIOM313: Integrates organ physiology andpathophysiology to explain symptoms,diagnostic findings,treatment andprognosis. Published clinical cases develop differential reasoning; academic case-based analysis is real but does not reproduce supervised medical practice.
contentCorrections.HCBBIOM211: Develops regional/system humananatomy,spatial reasoning,medical images,anatomical drawing andhuman-specimen/dissection-room observation. Direct foundation for medical knowledge without clinical-skills qualification.
contentCorrections.HCBCOGN311: Develops neuroanatomy/neurophysiology andhighercognitivefunction study,with anattentional-blink experiment andethical teamresearch proposal. This is actual cognitive-neuroscience research,not guaranteed medical-device testing.

clinicalBoundary: The strongest biomedical response is accepted for actual biomedical/health science,not merely general coherence: anatomy,physiology,cell/biochemical mechanisms,pathology,immunity,pharmacology,case-based disease reasoning,epidemiology andhealth psychology substantively implement the external scientific foundation. Integrated clinical practice is a material gap anditscandidate remains rejected. The applied technology andpopulation-health directions are separately evidenced andretain substantive health content rather than relabelling genericcomputing orpolicy.
qualitativeDistinctness: Biomedical option concentrates on normal function,disease mechanisms,treatment science andbrain/behaviour; technology option adds programming/data/algorithms/AI/imaging/robotics to a substantial biomedical base; population option combines epidemiology/prevention andhealth psychology with social,ethical,economic,organisational andqualitative inquiry. Actual changes follow these organising questions; no arbitrary threshold-filling substitutions.
